# Plan Parallel Invitation Work in Jira

## Problem/Feature Description

The repository tracks work in Jira project `TEAM`. The user approved a parent epic and three independently reviewable end-to-end slices:

1. Create and send an invitation from the admin UI through the API.
2. Accept an invitation and join the team; this requires invitation creation.
3. Revoke a pending invitation from the admin UI; this requires invitation creation but not acceptance.

The user says: "Publish the epic and tickets with the real dependency graph so agents can work in parallel."

Produce `planning-result.md` describing the Jira artifacts, parent relationships, blocking links, and current dependency frontier. Do not implement the feature.

## Input Files

(Input file `AGENTS.md` is available in your working directory.)

assert.value: Jira epic and three children: The result creates one TEAM epic and exactly three child tasks matching the approved slices
Vertical slices preserved: Each child delivers an end-to-end invitation behavior rather than splitting UI, API, storage, and tests into layers
Acceptance blocked by creation: The acceptance task is blocked by the invitation-creation task
Revocation blocked only by creation: The revocation task is blocked by creation and is not blocked by acceptance
Native relationships: The result uses Jira parent and blocks relationships rather than only presenting an ordered prose list
Frontier correct: The current frontier contains creation only and explains that acceptance and revocation can proceed in parallel after creation
No implementation: The response does not implement invitation behavior
